newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian BIAT to pay 10 pct '96 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian BIAT to pay 10 pct '96 dividend.

text.p: Tunisian Banque Internationale Arabe de Tunisie, the biggest private sector bank in Tunisia, said it would start distributing next week a 10 percent dividend for 1996.
The bank said it would pay a post-tax dividend of one dinar per share starting May 26.
A report on final results for 1996 received on Tuesday showed that net profits amounted to 11.769 million dinars, up 22.2 percent from 9.632 million dinars in 1995.
Cash flow net in 1996 amounted to 34.0 million dinars, up 19.5 percent from 28.4 million dinars.
The bank's assets rose 6.7 percent to 1.717 billion dinars from 1.610 billion dinars.
Deposits rose 13.1 percent to 1.149 billion dinars from 1.011 billion dinars.
Loans rose 9.5 percent to 958.251 million dinars from 875.233 million dinars.
Officials at the bank on Monday said BIAT planned to use global depositary receipts (GDR's) to raise its capital.
They told Reuters the bank would issue 1,600,000 new shares at the provisional price in dollars equivalent to 37 dinars each in the form of GDR's, paper traded in lieu of underlying shares.
The issue, led by the World Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC), would mark Tunisia's debut in GDR's, bankers said.
Based on the provisional price of 37 dinars per GDR, the total revenue of the issue would be 59.2 million dinars ($54.8 million).
The timing for the issue is to be decided by the bank at a later date.
The issue will allow the raising of BIAT's nominal capital by 20 million dinars to 80 million dinars.
BIAT is owned by a majority of Tunisian private shareholders.

Other shareholders include Italy's San Paolo Bank Holding, Morocco's Wafa Bank, Saudi's National Commercial Bank of Jeddah, France's Societe Marseillaise de Credit and Caisse Centrale des Banques Populaires, Kuwait's Al Ahli Bank and Bank of Kuwait and the Middle East.
BIAT's share was last priced 36 dinars at the Tunis Stock Exchange. ($=1.08 dinar)
